## Work log

<!-- Chronological, written as you go. What was actually done, why, what it cost.
     Reference commits and link to plans and notes. Prose beats a checklist here —
     this is the part you will actually reread in three months. -->

- Project brief: a comic page maker with three layers. First, a panel grid (default 3×4) whose
  cells merge contiguously, with panels breaking out of the frame as on the _Understanding
  Comics_ pp. 6 and 58 references. Second, per-panel images, mostly AI-generated. Third,
  WYSIWYG text per panel treated as a web layout: captions, speech and thought bubbles, SFX.
  Started by assessing nadiio's `canvas-tool-template` branch as a base.
- Assessed `canvas-tool-template`. It is one commit (`f07f230`, 2026-02-11): SvelteKit 2 +
  Svelte 5, Svelte Flow, Supabase auth + JSONB graph auto-save, command-pattern undo/redo, and
  shadcn-svelte. It is about 7 months behind nadiio `main`. Verdict: the shell, auth, persistence
  and undo patterns are reusable. The Svelte Flow canvas is the wrong primitive for a fixed page
  of panels, and there is no resizing, rich text, image storage or export. So the canvas layer
  gets written from scratch.
- Decided on a fresh SvelteKit app over forking the template, local-first for v1 (IndexedDB, no
  accounts). Wrote [the v1 plan](../plans/2026-09-28_comic-page-editor-v1.plan.md). Panels are
  cell sets traced to SVG polygons, because CSS Grid spans can't do L-shapes. Balloons live on
  the page rather than in panels, because they cross borders. The AI provider is an open
  question and only blocks the last task.
- Task 1: scaffolded with `sv create` (SvelteKit 2.63, Svelte 5.56, Vite 8, Tailwind 4, Vitest 4,
  Playwright). Its Prettier pass reformatted the diary markdown and its `.gitignore` dropped
  `.claude/settings.local.json`. I reverted both and added `/plans/` and `/work-diary/` to
  `.prettierignore`, since the diary script owns those files' generated sections. Ported
  HistoryManager and BatchCommand, and added `record()` so a drag becomes one undo step.
- Tasks 2–5 landed: the document model, grid geometry, panel commands and the editor shell. The
  panel outline is traced along the grid lattice rather than built from CSS Grid spans, so an
  L-shape is one 6-vertex polygon. `canMerge` rejects rings and corner pinches, which settled
  the "holes" open question: every panel has exactly one boundary loop. Two surprises. My first
  geometry fixture was arithmetically wrong (a 1000-wide page can't fit 4 × 220 cells), and the
  tests caught it. And `bind:clientWidth` never updated inside the flex layout, which left
  fit-to-view clamped at 5%; a ResizeObserver attachment fixed it. Verified in Chrome: merged a
  2×2 block and an L by keyboard, undid and redid, and got the "must share an edge" refusal. ⌘M
  became M because Chrome on macOS minimises the window on ⌘M.
- Tasks 6–7: free panels (a generic Transformer handles move and resize for panels now, and
  balloons later) and images (IndexedDB blobs, fill/fit, and an image mode with a ghosted
  full-image preview, wheel zoom at the pointer, keyboard pan and zoom). **Correction to the
  entry above:** the fit-to-view bug was not `bind:clientWidth`. The Chrome tab was hidden
  (`visibilityState: hidden`), and ResizeObserver callbacks are not delivered to hidden tabs.
  Fixed properly by measuring once up front. The same hidden tab made the automation tool's
  clicks unreliable, so the image flow was verified with dispatched pointer, keyboard and drop
  events. Also fixed: after M, focus was lost because the focused cell's polygon had been
  removed, so it now moves to the merged panel.
- Tasks 8–11: balloons (six shape types; stroke-first then fill-on-top so ellipse + tail read as
  one outline), TipTap in-place text, IndexedDB autosave plus multi-page, and PNG/PDF export.
  Two bugs worth remembering. First, the TipTap attachment read `balloon.h` while mounting, so
  auto-growing the balloon re-ran the attachment, which remounted TipTap, which grew the balloon
  again. That infinite loop froze the Chrome tab and wedged the browser extension; the fix was
  `untrack()`. After that I switched verification to headless Playwright, which also sidesteps
  the hidden-tab focus problems. Second, the exported PNG read "ELLO RIVER!": the test typed
  before TipTap's next-tick autofocus. It was a test race rather than a product bug, and the test
  now waits for focus. The first PDF also had a trailing blank sheet from `break-after` on the
  last page. Viewing the exported PNG confirmed the image, Comic Neue lettering and Bangers SFX
  are all embedded.
- New brief: log in, deploy on Vercel, Supabase on the free tier, and an MCP server. Decided
  with the user: their own supabase.com account, email + password, full-editing MCP tools, and
  OAuth for MCP so it works as a claude.ai connector. Checked current Supabase docs: the OAuth
  2.1 server (beta, all plans) does dynamic client registration, and the app supplies the consent
  page. Wrote [the plan](../plans/2026-09-28_accounts-cloud-mcp.plan.md). The deciding design
  point: the model layer is already framework-free, so the MCP tools run the same command classes
  as the editor, guarded by a `rev` column for optimistic concurrency and a conflict banner.
- Accounts work, in order:
  - The Vercel project `riverbanks-generator` is in the `yanthibicos-projects` team. The first
    `vercel deploy` was **promoted to production**, not preview, so the local-first v1 has been
    public at riverbanks-generator.vercel.app since then. I told the user.
  - Ops layer plus `/mcp`: 18 tools, a resource, and OAuth protected-resource metadata. Tested
    through the SDK's in-memory client and by calling the route directly.
  - Local Supabase took four attempts. CLI 2.95 gives up on the storage container's first health
    check too early, and analytics/vector were flaky, so analytics is off and I started with
    `--ignore-health-check`. The fault was never our migration: it failed with the migration
    removed too.
  - Integration tests against the stack pass: rev guard, RLS between two users, storage folders,
    and JWKS verification of a real ES256 token.
  - Auth e2e passes: sign-up with the confirmation email read from Mailpit, cloud save and
    reload, sign-out and the route guard, a cross-account 404, and the password reset. Two slips
    on the way: SvelteKit forbids a default action next to named ones, and the test pressed N
    before hydration.
  - MCP edits reached the database, but the open editor got no Realtime update. The cause was not
    ES256 (a Node probe with an ES256 token received events fine). The browser client subscribed
    before restoring its session from cookies, so it joined as anon and RLS dropped every event.
    Fixed by awaiting `getSession()` and calling `realtime.setAuth()` first.
  - The user redirected mid-flow: no emails at all (an internal seapunk-team tool), admins create
    accounts, and the cosmolocalcnx `riverbanks/` material is copied here. That folder is
    gitignored in its source repo because it names people, and this repo is public, so the copy is
    gitignored too (confirmed with the user). One mistake: `[auth.email] enable_signup = false`
    disables email **sign-in**; only `[auth] enable_signup` was needed.
  - Flaky e2e under parallel load had three causes:
    - A real product bug: autosave was scheduled from an `$effect` a tick late, so "Saved" showed
      before the save and a quick reload could lose the edit. Now scheduled synchronously, plus a
      beforeunload guard.
    - Tests filled forms before hydration (Svelte resets bound inputs), fixed with a
      `body[data-hydrated]` marker.
    - ⌘B landed inside ProseMirror's async `selectionchange` gap.
  - Port 4173 belonged to another project's preview server and 5173 to a dev server for this repo
    that I didn't start. Neither was touched; e2e moved to 4318, and the OAuth test follows
    Supabase's site_url redirect itself.
  - OAuth consent page plus a full client-side OAuth e2e test (discovery → dynamic registration →
    PKCE → consent → token → /mcp).
  - Production: the user created `riverbanks-comics` (krugthurasfvthjtchqo, Tokyo) and linked it.
    `db push` applied the migration, Vercel env vars are set, and `vercel deploy --prod` is live.
    Smoke checks pass. Its JWKS was already ES256, and dynamic registration is now on. **Public
    sign-up was still enabled** at deploy time (`/auth/v1/settings` shows disable_signup false),
    so I flagged it to the user.
- Later: palette v1 plus story drafts from the 2 PM Granola call, published as a private page for
  the team ("Blue Rivers Exhibit Book"). Then a plan for ChatGPT access to `/mcp`:
  [chatgpt-mcp-access](../plans/2026-09-28_chatgpt-mcp-access.plan.md). OpenAI's current docs
  require the MCP server to verify token audience from the `resource` parameter. It's unknown
  whether Supabase's OAuth server puts `resource` into `aud`, so the plan starts with a spike on a
  real ChatGPT connection before any code.
- ChatGPT access, done in one sitting:
  - The spike on production went through Yan's ChatGPT Plus. The plugin client is
    `codex-mcp-client`; it uses Streamable HTTP and DCR. Its token has `aud: "authenticated"`,
    because Supabase ignores `resource`, and it carries `client_id`.
  - So `/mcp` now requires `client_id`, which refuses web-session tokens.
  - Added tool annotations; `search` and `fetch` in OpenAI's schemas (a comic as a script, with
    balloons placed by panel outline, since cell lookup put a gutter-centred caption in no panel);
    and `whoami` with `openai/profile`.
  - Also fixed a live-update race: an edit landing before the Realtime join was missed; the editor
    now catches up on SUBSCRIBED and exposes `data-live`.
  - Verified in ChatGPT: list and create work. Confirmation behaviour, delete, deep research and
    reconnect are still to check.
- Re-tested the MCP from Claude Code against production: all 21 tools pass on a throwaway comic
  (since deleted), with correct guard errors for a grid change over merged panels and an unknown id.
  One real gap: an image URL that redirects failed as `fetch failed`, because `redirect: 'error'`
  was the SSRF guard. Now redirects are followed by hand, each hop re-checked against the same
  guard, and network errors name the host. A live picsum redirect loads through it.
